quizzes.title: 2026 Election Results: Practice MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Bangladesh has completed its 13th General Election, a contest that marks a major turning point in national politics. The vote came after roughly eighteen months of upheaval. That upheaval was led by students, and an interim arrangement governed the country for a period before the election. The result has ended a long stretch in which a single party held the country's politics in a firm grip, and the booklet presents it as a major political shift.

Tarique Rahman, who had emerged as the top leader of his party, has now taken office as Prime Minister. He took the oath at a formal ceremony in the capital, and the event was attended by a guest. He is the child of two former leaders of the country, and his arrival in power follows the overthrow of the government that preceded it.

The new government therefore begins its work after a period of intense change in national life. Several parties have won seats in the new legislature, and the composition of the house reflects the outcome of the vote. The previous Prime Minister had left the country after the uprising. The booklet records these events in one sequence, from the upheaval to the new administration.

questions.q: Which party, led by Tarique Rahman, won the 13th General Election in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, led by Tarique Rahman, won the 13th General Election.

questions.q: Where did Tarique Rahman take the oath of office as Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: The booklet says he took the oath at Parliament South Plaza in Dhaka.

questions.q: Whose two-decade dominance over Bangladeshi politics did the 2026 election end?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the election ended the Awami League's two-decade dominance.

questions.q:
Consider the assertion and reason below.
Assertion (A): Bangladesh's legislature is unicameral.
Reason (R): 300 members are elected directly through the first-past-the-post system.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but direct election by first-past-the-post does not explain why the legislature has one house.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Bangladesh Nationalist Party   ->   A. 209 seats
II. Jamaat-e-Islami   ->   B. 68 seats
III. National Citizen Party   ->   C. 6 seats
IV. Reserved seats for women   ->   D. 50 seats
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the BNP 209 seats, Jamaat-e-Islami 68, the National Citizen Party 6, and 50 seats reserved for women.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2026 Bangladesh election:
I. Om Birla attended the swearing-in ceremony of the new Prime Minister.
II. Jamaat-e-Islami won more seats than the Bangladesh Nationalist Party.
III. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party was founded in 1978.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while Jamaat-e-Islami won 68 seats against the BNP's 209.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Tarique Rahman succeeded the government of Sheikh Hasina.
II. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party won 68 seats in the 2026 election.
III. Tarique Rahman is the son of Ziaur Rahman.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the BNP won 209 seats, not 68.

quizzes.title: Political Transitions: Practice MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in the early 1970s, and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became the country's first Prime Minister after that. He later changed the constitution, and he also became head of state himself. The years that followed brought a sharp change in political life, and several of the country's leaders died violently. Some of these deaths took place during military actions, and army officers were involved in some of the incidents.

Power then passed between different leaders and parties over the following decades. One leader who held the presidency announced elections, which prepared the way for the next general election. That same leader was later killed during an attempted coup.

The most recent phase followed large public protests. A leader who had governed for a long time left the country, and an interim government led by Muhammad Yunus then took charge of the country's affairs.

The booklet traces these changes through a series of dated events, which together show how leadership and political structures shifted over several decades. Each change is linked to a specific period, and the sequence of transitions forms the background to the country's current politics. Each date in the booklet is tied to a named leader or event, which helps place the changes in order.

questions.q: After amending the constitution, which system of government did Sheikh Mujibur Rahman implement?
questions.explanation: The booklet says he amended the constitution, implemented a Presidential System and became President himself.

questions.q: In which city was President Ziaur Rahman assassinated during an attempted coup?
questions.explanation: The booklet says he was assassinated in Chittagong by army personnel during an attempted coup.

questions.q: Which period followed the student-led revolution and Sheikh Hasina's flight to India?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the interim period from 2024 to 2026 after the student-led revolution and Hasina's flight to India.

questions.q:
Consider the assertion and reason below.
Assertion (A): The 1975 amendment created a single-party system in Bangladesh.
Reason (R): All other political parties were abolished, and leaders were mandated to join BAKSAL.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the abolition of other parties and the mandate to join BAKSAL is what made the 1975 amendment a single-party system.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Bangladesh gained independence from Pakistan   ->   A. 1971
II. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated   ->   B. 1975
III. Ziaur Rahman was assassinated   ->   C. 1981
IV. Sheikh Hasina was sworn in as Prime Minister for the first time   ->   D. 1996
questions.explanation: The booklet dates independence to 1971, Mujibur Rahman's assassination to 1975, Ziaur Rahman's to 1981, and Hasina's first swearing-in to 1996.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bangladesh's political history:
I. Ziaur Rahman became President in 1977.
II. Khaleda Zia was sworn in as Prime Minister for the first time on 23 June 1996.
III. The Awami League won 293 of the 300 seats in the 1973 parliamentary elections.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the 23 June 1996 swearing-in belongs to Sheikh Hasina.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became Prime Minister in 1972.
II. The BNP last governed Bangladesh during 2001-2006.
III. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated in 1981.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated in 1975, not 1981.

quizzes.title: India-Bangladesh Ties: Practice MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Relations between India and Bangladesh have passed through several phases, shaped by security concerns, trade and the approach of successive governments. Some periods were difficult, while others saw closer cooperation. The relationship has therefore been closely tied to the leadership in Dhaka at each stage.

Trade is central to the relationship. Cooperation extends to infrastructure, energy and defence, and both sides have pursued connectivity projects such as road and rail links. Visa arrangements also matter to citizens who travel for healthcare and tourism, and the visa systems have been improved to support such travel.

Security is central to the present agenda. The booklet lists several priorities for the new government. These include managing political pressure over a former leader's presence in India, preventing a drift of Bangladesh toward other partners, and countering extremism and insurgency that threatens stability. Together these priorities link diplomacy with domestic politics.

After a period of sharp public feeling in Bangladesh, the relationship is being reshaped. Many citizens viewed India's support for a previous administration with suspicion, and the new government must balance these views with the need to keep trade and connectivity running smoothly. The booklet presents these issues together, so trade, security and connectivity are discussed as parts of one relationship.

questions.q: Which bridge, built over the Feni River, connects Sabroom in Tripura with Ramgarh in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Bharat Bangla Maitri Bridge as built over the Feni River, connecting Sabroom with Ramgarh.

questions.q: Which joint army exercise is conducted between India and Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Sampriti as the army joint exercise, while Bongosagar is the navy exercise.

questions.q: What was the value of India-Bangladesh trade in FY 2023-24?
questions.explanation: The booklet records trade in FY 2023-24 at US$ 14.01 billion.

questions.q:
Consider the assertion and reason below.
Assertion (A): India's relations with Bangladesh were strained during the 2001-2006 BNP-led government.
Reason (R): India accused that regime of sheltering North-East insurgent groups.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet links the strained ties of 2001-2006 to India's accusation that the regime sheltered insurgent groups.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Land Boundary Agreement   ->   A. 2015
II. Interim period of anti-India sentiment   ->   B. 2024-2026
III. 'Golden Chapter' under Sheikh Hasina   ->   C. 2009-2024
IV. BNP-led government with Jamaat-e-Islami   ->   D. 2001-2006
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Land Boundary Agreement to 2015, the Golden Chapter to 2009-2024, the interim period to 2024-2026, and the BNP-led government to 2001-2006.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India-Bangladesh relations:
I. Security priorities include preventing Bangladesh from drifting toward Pakistan or China.
II. The Bharat Bangla Maitri Bridge was built over the Teesta River.
III. Duty-free access on tariff lines has been expanded through the South Asian Free Trade Area Agreement.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while the bridge is over the Feni River, not the Teesta.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. India and Bangladesh established diplomatic relations in 1971.
II. The Kolkata-Dhaka-Agartala bus service began in 2015.
III. The Bongosagar exercise is an army exercise between India and Bangladesh.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Bongosagar is a navy exercise.
